we have proposed a 100 MHz fully-integrated buck DC-DC converter with standard package-bondwire inductors, which achieves 1.2-A output current with 82.4 % efficiency and 0.96-A/mm2 current density.
the proposed design can achieve 82.4 % efficiency with 1.25mm2 chip area and 0.96A/mm2 current density.
a four-phase fully-integrating buck converter with package bondwire inductor and flying capacitor is presented.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chip area and cost reduction of fully-integrated DC-DC converters by utilizing standard package-bondwire inductors, which has not been addressed in the previous work.

the design and analysis of a fully integrated four-phase buck converter with standard bondwire inductivity and CFLY topology, which can be easily integrated into the system-on-chip (SoC) and achieve a high current density and high efficiency.
the fully-integrated converter with the chip-area and cost penalty minimized.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this work is the first demonstration of a fully-integrated buck regulator with package-bondwire inductance and a simple yet effective CFLY topology, and it is a promising solution for the future high current density and fully-integrated power management ICs.
this paper presents a 1.2-A 82.4%-efficiency fully-integrated buck DC/DC converter with standard package-bondwire inductors in 0.25 mm2 chip-area.
the presented four-phase fully-integratable buck converter with the flying capacitor topology is a promising candidate for future high-efficiency and high-density power delivery system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the four-phase operation and the CFLY topology can be used to reduce the cost and increase the current density of the fully-integrated converters.
the proposed fully-integrated buck converters are the most efficient and smallest fully-integrated converters with the highest current density reported to date.
the proposed fully-integrated buck topology is suitable for high efficiency and high current density applications with the area penalty minimized.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed design is able to reduce the area of the power stage significantly by utilizing the parasitic bond wire inductance at input and package inductance at output.

, by utilizing the parasitic bond-wires inductances, the chip-area hungry on-chip integrated inductors and capacitors can be eliminated, and the fully-integrated converter can be made with a much smaller chip-area, while the current density is also significantly increased.
the fully-integrated converter is not only a promising candidate for the next generation of power converters, but also a promising way to reduce chip area and cost.
